articles.headline: Mavericks lean into Cooper Flagg's peanut butter and jelly trend with pop-up
articles.description: The Dallas Mavericks' pop-up includes creamy peanut butter and grape jelly on white sourdough bread.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks fans might not be able to hoop like Cooper Flagg, but they can eat like him.

The Mavericks announced Thursday that they are bringing "The Jam Box" pop-up concession stand to American Airlines Center exclusively for Saturday's game against the LA Clippers, courtesy of Levy Restaurants.

Fans will be able to indulge in the limited-edition offering of creamy peanut butter and grape jelly on white sourdough bread -- Flagg's preferred combination. They are set to be priced at $3.20, a nod to Flagg's No. 32, with just 320 sandwiches supplied and given out in a sandwich bag sealed with a sticker. They are available while supplies last on the American Airlines Center's main plaza level outside section 117.

The forward has been spotted eating the combination on the bench during games and even in news conferences this season. He explained on Nov. 8 that the in-game snack is because he's trying to put on weight and gain muscle.

"So those requirements I got to meet. I'm just trying to stay ahead of it," Flagg said. "We got another game [on Nov. 9]. So just trying to get my calories and stay ahead of it and be ready for another one."

He clarified that he's a smooth peanut butter and grape jelly enthusiast, no different than what the Mavericks are giving away Saturday. Flagg added that he also enjoys a simple peanut butter and banana sandwich, while sometimes adding honey.

The 19-year-old is currently averaging 24.2 points, 6.6 rebounds and 6.4 assists per game. As his PB&J trend gained traction, Flagg dropped 43 points, 10 rebounds and six assists in a 125-122 win against the Indiana Pacers on Nov. 9. He then forgot to bring his sandwich to the postgame news conference, before posting an image of it while in his car.

NBA players and peanut butter and jelly sandwiches might be the epitome of the saying: "we go together like peanut butter and jelly." During his tenure with the Boston Celtics in the 2007-08 campaign, Kevin Garnett ate a sandwich before a game, proceeded to play well and started a tradition that other NBA players have adopted since then.

Now, Mavs fans can potentially start their own.

articles.headline: Washington Commanders unveil 'Beer Spear' ahead of 'Hail Raiser' debut on 'MNF'
articles.description: The limited-edition collectible vessel can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it.
articles.body:
Monday marks the Washington Commanders' debut of their new alternate uniforms, the "Hail Raiser." The Commanders will be ringing in the all-black threads with a similarly themed concession item: the "Beer Spear."

It's a limited-edition collectible vessel that can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it. Featured on the vessel is the Commanders' new W-spear logo, which also appears on the Hail Raiser helmet. The logo includes a gold spear interwoven into a burgundy "W" with gold outline.

The Commanders announced the new item Thursday. It will be available for purchase at select concession stands during the rest of the Commanders' home games, starting on "Monday Night Football" against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Washington already boasts a crab stuffed pretzel at its concession stands. The pretzel is shaped like a crab and is filled with lemon tarragon crab dip topped with garlic butter and grated parmesan cheese.

The beer spear is just another in the list of creative sport-related concession items that deal with beer. Some MLB teams have the "beer bat." The NHL's Buffalo Sabres introduced the "beer sabres" last season, while the Philadelphia Flyers countered with the "beer skate." Each of them became instantly popular among fans and collectors alike.

Teams haven't stopped experimenting for similar items, and with a beer spear now off the table, the natural evolution could be a beer shield.

articles.headline: Sam Hartman's next drive: 'The Bachelor' questions answered
articles.description: A guide to the Commanders quarterback's upcoming search for love and how his NFL commitments could shape the season.
articles.body:
At the Washington Commanders' Thursday practice, a dozen or so cameras trained on the club's fourth quarterback. Normally, this player would be ignored during a shooting period, but Washington's fourth quarterback is Sam Hartman, who despite having never played in an NFL regular-season game, will be the next lead of "The Bachelor" in the 30th season of the show.

After a good throw, Hartman said to the other three quarterbacks: "I hope they post that one."

At the end of the throwing session, a Commanders player said to the media focused on Hartman, "Do you guys want a hair flip?"

When Hartman, the practice squad quarterback known for his movie-star quality hair, was announced as the next Bachelor last week, he became the second active NFL player to take the lead title. His short and sweet "Good Morning America" appearance left both football and "The Bachelor" fans with many pressing questions and hilarious hypotheticals. 

What happens if the 3-5-1 Commanders miraculously make the postseason and they need Hartman but he has to go film "The Bachelor"? With the show premiering on March 21, just 10 weeks after Week 18 and nine weeks after the wild-card round, will Hartman have to leave for the Bachelor mansion in California to begin filming? Though Hartman hasn't played in a regular-season game, he has served as the emergency third quarterback for a stretch in each of the past two seasons, and with the state of the Commanders' often-injured quarterbacks room, does this production schedule mean the backup to the backup position could end up in jeopardy? (this might seem farfetched but the Commanders played their third-in-line quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis in London this season, when starter Jayden Daniels was out and then backup Marcus Mariota got hurt).

And "The Bachelor" franchise has historically had a no phones policy for participants. While Hartman will not be demanding a huge crowd of clubs in free agency, how will he stay updated of any new offers if he finishes the season on the practice squad and becomes a street free agent? Will he have his phone to talk to his agent?

Fear not, for Hartman addressed the media Thursday after practice and ESPN has attempted to answer these extremely urgent questions for the sake of Commanders fans and contestants vying for his attention, who might be curious about his NFL obligations and financial status going forward.

Let's start with the basics.

How did he become a candidate for "The Bachelor"?

Hartman told reporters Thursday that ABC reached out to him, "just kind of out of the blue." He said Wake Forest is a "pipeline" for "The Bachelor."

Hartman is the third Wake Forest football alumni to participate in "The Bachelor" franchise. Matt James and Tyler Cameron also played for Wake Forest.

The ACC Network called Wake Forest "Bachelor U" on Instagram after Hartman's announcement.

articles.headline: NFL Week 11 uniforms: Texans debut Rivalries look, Commanders rock 'Hail Raiser'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 11, led by Houston debuting its Rivalries combination.
articles.body:
A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

It's the Texans' turn first, as they will wear their Rivalries threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

For the first time, the Texans will wear a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture. 

As part of the Commanders' redesign of their uniform closet last offseason, they unveiled the all-black "Hail Raiser" alternates, which debut against the Cincinnati Bengals on "Monday Night Football." It features a black helmet with a "Spear W" logo on both sides, as the spear and "W" are interwoven at their center. Burgundy and gold stripes appear on the sleeve and pants, while the lid includes a three-stripe look on top of similar colors. Solid burgundy block numbers are outlined by gold. 

The Buffalo Bills are also rocking a Rivalries look against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo debuted its all-white "Cold Front" combination last season, but it returns with icy details throughout. The shoulder sleeve features a chrome charging buffalo, the first time a Bills uniform incorporates this element. The white helmet similarly includes a frosty metallic-filled charging buffalo logo, while the shoulder and pant leg patters boast a cracked-ice texture with a pattern that resembles snowfall on a bison's fur. 

It's an alternate week for the Detroit Lions as well. Detroit is going all-black against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Complete with a Honolulu blue matte helmet, the "Motor City Muscle" threads were first unveiled in 2024. The lid also includes a leaping lion logo in silver with a black stripe down the middle. The Lions wore these threads in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers.

articles.headline: The Steelers last won in Philadelphia in 1965. Can they top an Eagles team on 7-game losing streak?
articles.description: — Perhaps the Steelers should have stayed attached at the hip pads with the Eagles — as they were when they merged for the 1943 season to form the Steagles — to avoid such an ignominious losing streak in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Perhaps the Steelers should have stayed attached at the hip pads with the Eagles — as they were when they merged for the 1943 season to form the Steagles — to avoid such an ignominious losing streak in Philadelphia.


              Pittsburgh's losing streak in Philly spans 11 games over six decades, three stadiums, four Steelers coaches including Chuck Noll, Bill Cowher and Mike Tomlin and has even predated — wait for it — the Super Bowl.


              That's right, the Steelers haven't won in Philadelphia since 1965. The first Super Bowl was played after the 1966 season on Jan. 15, 1967.


              Philadelphia beat Pittsburgh on Dec. 4, 1966, the first of four straight wins at Franklin Field. The Steelers won three more times at Veterans Stadium and all four games at their current home, Lincoln Financial Field.


              The average margin of victory for the Eagles over the last three games (2016, 2022 and 2024) is 22.3 points, while the overall margin of victory since the streak started is 11.7 points.


              “We feel like we need to take care of that,” coach Mike McCarthy said.


              Good news for the Steelers: This should be their best chance to win in Philly in years, even as Pittsburgh is reeling from a 38-18 beatdown at the hands of Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and the scorching Cincinnati Bengals.


              The Steelers are the betting favorite to win Sunday and snap the streak, and for good reason. 


              This anticipated showdown when the NFL schedule dropped has instead turned into such a must-miss contest as the Eagles slog through a seven-game losing streak that the game was bumped from the national TV window to a pedestrian 1 p.m. EST kickoff.


              If a losing streak falls in Philadelphia, and no one is around to watch it, does it count?


              “I’d have to look and really study to see what those glaring weaknesses are,” Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward said. “But a lot of respect for what they got over there. They’ve won Super Bowls, they’ve had some really good teams, some really great fronts, so we’re going to have our hands full.”


              While Pittsburgh appears plenty capable of reaching the playoffs for the sixth time in seven seasons, the Eagles are set for their first losing season under sixth-year coach Nick Sirianni. 


              Sirianni promised a deep dive into the Eagles' woes during their bye week and returned with no obvious answers. He reaffirmed his commitment to quarterback Joe Milton for a second straight game — replacing the ineffective Tanner McKee, who replaced the injured Jalen Hurts — and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion remains the play-caller even as he leads one of the worst offenses in the NFL.

articles.headline: Sources: Spurs' Dylan Harper out 1-3 weeks with hip strain
articles.description: Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday.

This type of strain will carry a one-to-three-week timetable for return, dependent on Harper's rehab.

Harper was injured when he appeared to slip on a wet spot in the team's 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons in San Antonio on Tuesday night. Harper writhed on the floor in pain after the play and appeared to grab at his groin area.

"The visuals and optics of falls, potential injuries, whatever you want to call it can be impressionable. And that one did not look great," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

"So, there's a lot of WebMD and you try not to let your mind run the wrong way and you hope for the best," he continued. "But you really don't know. It's part of the things we can't control. So, we're just very lucky, fortunate and mostly just happy for Dylan that there will be some time [that he's out]. Very best case scenario for a lot of the things that could have been."

Teammates Keldon Johnson and David Jones Garcia initially escorted Harper to the tunnel before the second-year guard put his arm over the shoulder of a staffer who helped him down the hallway.

Harper is averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 15 games this season.

articles.headline: Commanders' defense preparing for high-flying Bengals offense
articles.description: — Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn knows the challenge facing his defense for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- — Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn knows the challenge facing his defense for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.


              When asked on Thursday why Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense has been so good this season against the blitz, Quinn chuckled.


              “I feel like they’ve been good against everything right now,” Quinn said.


              Washington's head coach certainly has reason to feel that way.


              The Bengals are coming off a 38-18 drubbing of the Steelers and have scored at least 31 points in their past five games, and in six of their nine games this season. They currently rank third in the NFL in points per game (30.9).


              Led by Burrow and the one-two punch at receiver of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, the Bengals have proven to be one of the league's best teams once again on the back of its offense. 


              Burrow has a 74.7% completion rate, is second in the league in yards at 2,795 and first in touchdown passes at 27.


              “He’s decisive,” Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves said. “He’s one of the guys that gets the ball out of his hands quick and trusts what he sees. At the same time, he’s also just going to give his guys a chance. He trusts those two really well. He trusts all those guys really well. He’s going to give those guys the opportunity, and when he does, we got to make the plays that we’re able to make. One of the quickest release points in the game.”


              Burrow has relied on Chase and Higgins heavily so far this season, as they rank sixth and 11th in receptions, respectively, as well as fourth and sixth in yards.


              “Those dudes can run anything on the route tree," Reaves said. "They can line up anywhere. They present a challenge to any coverage, two-high, single-high (safety). They do a great job. We just got to be at our best when our best is required. They’re going to give those guys opportunities. Those dudes are two superstars in this business, so they’re going to have opportunities and when we get chances to make plays, we just want to make them.”


              After an important win over the Giants last week, the Commanders have their hands full against a Bengals team that is aiming for the top seed in the AFC.


              “It's a difficult challenge,” Quinn said. “The running back (Chase Brown) has targets, tight end (Mike Gesicki) does down in the red zone. So, everybody’s got difficult downs, so you can’t double up everybody. But you do have to take your shots of where to go and how to go about that. We’ll have our ways, but definitely one of the biggest challenges with them is multiple people, and performing at a high level.”

articles.headline: NFL Week 11 arrivals: C.J. Stroud leads the way ahead of Colts-Texans
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The forecast affects the game plan for how NFL players put together their Week 11 looks.

The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans kick things off Thursday night in Houston, where evening temperatures in the upper 60s should leave room for light layers.

However, Sunday's arrivals will call for a little more wardrobe strategy. 

With morning temperatures near freezing in Denver before an afternoon climb into the 40s, players arriving for Las Vegas Raiders-Denver Broncos have an opening for coats and chunky knits. Showers in Chicago could make weatherproof outerwear a smart finishing touch, while temperatures approaching 70 in Southern California give the New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers room to keep things lighter.

On the East Coast, Sunday's forecast leaves room for fall outfits without going full winter. Morning temperatures in the 50s in Buffalo should give Miami Dolphins and Buffalo Bills players an opening for sweaters and light jackets, while Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants arrivals in East Rutherford call for similar layers under cloudy skies, with rain possible later in the day.

From practical layers to outfits built for the spotlight, here are the standout arrivals from Week 11.

Thursday night fashion

Texture did the talking in C.J. Stroud 's arrival. The Texans quarterback sported a gray knit polo paired with relaxed light-wash jeans, while a black woven bag, brown shoes and a blue-faced watch added the finishing touches.

articles.headline: Thomas Frank eager to avoid repeat of Arsenal coffee cup controversy at Palace
articles.description: Thomas Frank said he hopes never to get caught drinking from a Brighton coffee cup after he was reminded of his famous gaffe from his time at Tottenham.
articles.body:
Thomas Frank said he hopes never to get caught drinking from a Brighton coffee cup after he was reminded of his famous gaffe from his time at Tottenham.

In January, the new Crystal Palace boss -- then in charge of Spurs -- was spotted sipping from a cup branded with the logo of their bitter rivals Arsenal ahead of their Bournemouth loss -- something he at the time insisted he simply did not notice, and would have been "absolutely stupid" to do.

Frank takes charge of the Premier League's bottom club for the first time on Saturday for what could be a crucial trip to Coventry, who sit one place clear of the relegation zone with two more points than the Danish club's new club.

- Predicting the rest of the Premier League season: How all 20 teams will finish

- Frank: Crystal Palace job 'too good' to turn down

Asked if there was a chance he might get busted with more controversial drinkware, Frank joked: "I hope not! I still think it's a fantastic story.

"I know, and I still don't understand, how anyone can think that I will drink from a cup from an opponent's team, that their supporters don't like, on purpose. Come on. But what a story, huh, to discuss?"

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal.

"If you don't learn from any of your jobs, I don't think you reflect, I don't think you improve, and I don't think you get better," said Frank, who was sacked by Spurs in February after less than eight months in charge.

"Of course there's a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I've learned, definitely."

Frank added that he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, "eating too well" and collecting passport stamps after his Spurs departure, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, "[It's] because you can't help yourself."

"I was very aware I didn't want to do anything in the summer," he said. "I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it's good to be back in the circus, but it's also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

"I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well [chairman] Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, [sporting director] Matt Hobbs and [recruitment consultant] Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea."

So pleased is Frank to be back, in fact, that he admitted: "I'm a little bit surprised by this feeling I have in the body, how good it feels."

Frank will be without Jean-Philippe Mateta, who will serve the second game of his three-match ban for the red card he was shown in Palace's loss to Frank's former employers Spurs before the international break.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's 1st Man United training session filmed by drone operator
articles.description: Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.
articles.body:
Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.

Around 12 minutes of the session was posted online on Thursday -- Pochettino's first full day in the job after arriving in Manchester on Wednesday. United have declined to comment.

- Pochettino: Man United players must relearn 'about being winners'

- Predicting the rest of the Premier League season: How all 20 teams will finish

- After a decade of near misses, Man United finally get their man in Pochettino

The footage shows Pochettino -- who signed a two-and-a-half year deal to take over from Michael Carrick last week -- working with a group of players while another two groups work separately under the supervision of his assistant, Jesus Perez.

Audio from the footage of United's Carrington training base could be heard, with the man appearing to operate the drone saying "let's get closer," before zooming in on Pochettino.

Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo were among the players shown working with Pochettinho.

"I can definitely see Harry Maguire," added the man providing commentary. "That there is Bruno [Fernandes], definitely, [I can] tell by the gestures."

Perez, along with staff members Toni Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino, arrived at Carrington earlier in the week after being released from their commitments with the USMNT ahead of Pochettino's final game in charge against Haiti on Tuesday.

The account justified the filming in a pinned post that said it's legal.

"It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone," the post said. "The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licenses, public liability and insurance required."

The post said no sensitive information had been revealed with regard to how struggling United would line up at fourth-place Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

"As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session," wrote the poster. "There are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."

Pochettino travelled directly from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final match with the USMNT and arrived at Carrington on Wednesday afternoon. His first game as United head coach is against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Arda Güler signs new six-year Real Madrid contract
articles.description: Arda Güler has signed a new, long-term contract at Real Madrid until 2032, the club said on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Arda Güler has signed a new, long-term contract at Real Madrid until 2032, the club said on Wednesday.

Midfielder Güler, 21, has been one of Madrid's outstanding players this season, starring under new coach José Mourinho.

Güler joined Madrid as a teenager in July 2023, and is already an established international with Türkiye.

"Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Güler have agreed to an extension of the player's contract, keeping him with the club until June 30, 2032," the club said on Wednesday.

"Over his four seasons wearing our jersey, he has made 126 appearances and won five trophies: one Champions League, one FIFA Club World Cup, one UEFA Super Cup, one LaLiga title, and one Spanish Supercopa.

"He is a Turkish international, having earned 38 caps for his national team to date.

"Last September, he received the Breakthrough Player of the Season award for the 2025-2026 Champions League."

Güler has made 12 appearances in LaLiga this season -- contributing three goals and four assists -- with Madrid currently second in the table, three points behind Barcelona.

- JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears

- Vinícius Júnior hits Brazil hat trick, vows to take form to Real Madrid

- Oviedo fan handed suspended prison sentence for racist abuse toward Mbappé

In the Champions League, he played a key role in Madrid's dramatic 4-3 comeback at AS Roma last month, coming off the bench to create two of the goals.

Güler played 90 minutes for Türkiye in both of their games during this international break, in defeats to Belgium and France.

He scored a sensational free kick against Belgium to give his side the lead.

What you need to know for Thursday

Karl-Anthony Towns has recorded double-doubles in each of his first 14 games this season, setting a New York Knicks franchise record. He is averaging 21.2 PPG and a league-leading 14.1 RPG. On Thursday, Towns visits his former team, the Minnesota Timberwolves, who remain without Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo. It's one of four games on the slate.

Victor Wembanyama finished with 25 points and 18 rebounds against the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, but the San Antonio Spurs had their 12-game winning streak snapped. San Antonio hosts the LA Clippers and will be without Dylan Harper and Tobias Harris.

The Memphis Grizzlies have won four straight, and Cam Spencer is coming off a 26-point, seven-assist performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday. The Golden State Warriors (8-7) haven't scored 100 points in three consecutive games without Stephen Curry. Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back.

Fantasy stream team

articles.headline: Valentín Barco on Chelsea career so far: 'I think I can give a lot more'
articles.description: Chelsea's Valentín Barco has said he is confident that he's still a long way away from reaching his full potential.
articles.body:
Chelsea's Valentín Barco has said he is confident that he's still a long way away from reaching his full potential.

The Argentina international returned to Chelsea this week having not featured in his country's two international friendlies, a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay and a 7-0 rout of Costa Rica.

"As a player, you always want to play so you are not happy when you don't but I understand this is the best national team in the world," Barco told ESPN. "But I'm happy to come to the national team, to continue to represent my country. I will now try to play at Chelsea and contribute."

Barco, 22, was part of Argentina's squad that finished runners-up to Spain at the 2026 World Cup.

He signed a contract with Chelsea through 2033 following his strong performances for Strasbourg, the club he joined from Brighton & Hove Albion in January 2025.

Returning to the Premier League was a priority for Barco, who made only seven appearances during his time at Brighton. Barco has had limited playing time under Xabi Alonso but said he believes he will eventually shine at Stamford Bridge.

"I think I can give a lot more," he said. "I also said the same thing when I was at Strasbourg; even when I was playing well, I knew I could give more because I know what I can give.

"I have a lot of confidence in myself so I have to keep working to continue growing."

Barco has one goal in even appearances, four of which in the Premier League.
